hypothesis: Among related teleost species (same family), relative body depth (depth/length) and relative body width (width/length) vary inversely, so that the length-weight coefficient k = W/L^3, a proxy for volume at a given length, varies less across species than either relative transverse dimension.
pass_criterion: Pre-registered. Species means from FishShapes v1 specimens (standard length SL, maximum body depth BD, maximum fish width FW, mass M; specimens with all four > 0). Variables per species: d = ln(BD/SL), w = ln(FW/SL), k = ln(M/SL^3). Families with >= 5 species are kept and each variable is centred on its family mean. (A) Spearman rho between family-centred d and w is < 0 with one-sided p < 0.05. (B) the SD of family-centred k is smaller than the SDs of family-centred d and of family-centred w. SUPPORTS if A and B both hold.
fail_criterion: Pre-registered. REFUTES if the Spearman rho between family-centred d and w is >= 0 AND the SD of family-centred k is >= the smaller of the SDs of family-centred d and w. Any other outcome is MIXED. Fewer than 20 qualifying families or 200 species: inconclusive (underpowered).
interpretation: Thompson's 'expansion in one transverse dimension compensated by compression in the other' is read as negative covariation of depth and width at a given length among related fishes; 'related' is operationalized as the same family (FishBase family names used in FishShapes). Length is standard length; 'thickness' is maximum fish width; 'volume at a given length' is mass/SL^3 (Thompson's k uses weight, so mass is the direct quantity). Family-centring removes between-family differences so that the comparison is among related species, as Thompson's haddock/plaice and shark/skate examples are. Because ln k is approximately d + w + ln(density x shape factor), condition B can hold only if d and w covary negatively; it is the 'volume less affected than the linear dimensions' clause. Secondary, reported but not part of the verdict: Thompson's named pair, plaice (Pleuronectes platessa) vs haddock (Melanogrammus aeglefinus), if both are in the data: depth ratio expected ~2, width ratio ~0.5, k ratio ~1. Note they are in different orders, so this pair is not 'related' by the family criterion.

test_contract.expected_observation: Within fish families, species that are relatively deeper are relatively narrower (negative family-centred correlation of ln(depth/SL) and ln(width/SL)), and ln(mass/SL^3) varies less than either.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: Relative depth and width covary positively or not at all within families, and mass/SL^3 varies at least as much as the less variable of the two transverse dimensions.
test_contract.admissible_datasets: Measurements of standard length, maximum body depth, maximum body width and mass taken on the same fish specimens, across many species in many families, by a source independent of Thompson; species identified to FishBase taxonomy; public licence.
test_contract.inference_method: Species means, family-centring for families with >= 5 species, Spearman correlation of centred ln depth ratio vs ln width ratio (one-sided test for negative), and comparison of the SDs of centred ln k vs centred ln depth and width ratios, against the pre-registered thresholds.

preregistration.species_mean: geometric mean over specimens of each measurement

datasets.name: FishShapes v1: functionally relevant measurements of teleost shape and size on three dimensions (Price et al. 2022)
datasets.license: CC0 1.0 (Dryad); the README asks users to cite Price et al. 2022, Ecology 103:e3829
datasets.files_note: Version zip containing FishShapes_specimensv1.csv (1,662,135 bytes, sha256 7447fdc92c5fd5c9ecf1d9713bbd4207d2de7ab4b2ea0e320871041da8e34264, matching Dryad's published digest; analysis.py checks it) and README.txt.
datasets.role: standard length, maximum body depth, maximum fish width and mass of 16,523 museum specimens (Smithsonian NMNH), 1-3 per species

method: analysis.py downloads the Dryad version zip, verifies the specimen CSV against Dryad's SHA-256 digest, keeps the 16,377 specimens with positive mass, SL, depth and width, and takes geometric species means (6,091 species). For the 5,670 species in the 195 families with >= 5 species it computes d = ln(depth/SL), w = ln(width/SL) and k = ln(mass/SL^3), centres each on its family mean, and computes the Spearman correlation of centred d and w and the SDs of centred d, w and k. Per-family correlations and SDs are written to derived/families.csv; the plaice/haddock ratios are reported separately.

measured.unit: Spearman rho between family-centred ln(body depth/SL) and ln(body width/SL) across teleost species

caveats: Within families, relatively deep species are also relatively wide, not narrower: the family-centred correlation is +0.53, positive in 90% of the 195 families (median +0.56). As a result ln k varies more (SD 0.35) than ln depth/SL (0.22) or ln width/SL (0.18), the opposite of Thompson's 'volume less affected than the linear dimensions'.

Both ratios are divided by standard length, so overall elongation (slender vs stocky species) makes them covary positively. The pre-registered test follows Thompson's own framing ('at a given length'), but it does not isolate depth-width compensation at fixed cross-sectional area; an analysis that removes elongation (e.g. using depth/width directly or a cross-section measure) was not pre-registered and was not run.

Thompson's named pair is partly borne out: plaice is 2.09 times as deep relative to length as haddock (expected ~2) and 0.64 times as wide (expected ~0.5, inside the pre-registered 0.35-0.7 band), but its k is 1.44 times haddock's, outside the pre-registered 0.8-1.25 'nearly equal' band. This pair is descriptive only and not part of the verdict.

Specimens are preserved museum fish; mass and width can change with fixation and ethanol storage, and specimens were chosen as adult-sized, not at matched length. These add noise to k but are unlikely to reverse the sign of a +0.53 correlation across 5,670 species.
Species means rest on 1-3 specimens; intraspecific variation and measurement error inflate all three SDs, and k (three measurements combined) gets the most.

preregistered_at is the time of the pre-registration commit (78fafafa); the committed pre-registration carried an estimated time (21:40Z) written before committing. The data were first downloaded after that commit; criteria are unchanged.
